newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on hot local money.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on hot local money.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up in morning trade on Friday as local banks poured in funds from the government securities market, while foreign investors focused on second-tier stocks, traders said.
They gave different opinions on where the market would move.
At 0845 national power utility UES ordinaries rose to $0.4318 from $0.4290 at Thursday's close, Sberbank rose to $309.00 from $295.50 and regional utility Mosenergo rose to $1.570 from $1.553.
Metals plant Norilsk Nickel, which soared on Thursday, eased to $17.75 from $18.20.

"Active buying started from the very morning, mostly from Russian operators," said Bank Rossiisky Kredit trader Andrei Girichev, adding the money came from Russian banks, which were shifting the funds from other markets.
Rye, Man and Gor Securities chief trader Igor Kozhechkin forecast the market would rise during the day.
"When there is so much money around, the market cannot fall," he said. "It will be up, only up."
But Girichev said Russian money may not be enough to provide for a sustained growth.
"The rise is mainly caused by Russian money, it is unclear for how long it will be able to fuel the rise," he said.
Kozhechkin said there was strong support for Rostelekom and other telecoms ahead of an auction for 25 plus one share stake in national telecoms holding Svyazinvest.
The results of the auction will be announced today.
Rostelekom rose to $4.84 from $4.71 and St Petersburg Telephone edged up to $2.25 from $2.17.
